2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

raw_response.chosen_tool: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable / Some spatial missingness concern: Individual panel attrition does not apply because the study uses repeated cross-sectional DHS waves rather than a longitudinal cohort; however, two of six geopolitical zones (Northcentral and Southsouth) were not surveyed in 1990, infrastructure items are absent in 1990, and spatial regression coverage drops from 1,415 total LGA-ethnic partitions to 685 available units (N = 631 with complete covariates in Tables 4-5) and N = 127-162 units in the 2012 Afrobarometer regressions (Tables 6-7).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: Serious / High concern for causal inference (Some concern for descriptive correlations): Tables 4-5 control for an extensive set of geographic, disease, population-density, petrol, and historical slave-export covariates (plus sensitivity checks excluding Lagos and the Southeast), but static cross-sectional OLS cannot separate post-1976 policy punishment from unobserved historical, cultural, religious, or state-level fiscal confounders correlated with precolonial centralization and >70% Muslim population share. In Table 7, cross-sectional regressions of 2013 service access on 2012 local government perceptions control only for population density, leaving substantial omitted-variable confounding and reverse causality unaddressed.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Weak: While the historical narrative identifies specific legal instruments (the 1907 Native Authority Proclamation and the 1976 Local Government Reform Law), legal exposure and statutory compliance are not directly coded or measured. Noncompliance with the 1976 Local Government Reform Law is proxied indirectly by interacting Murdock's c. 1850 centralization dummy with a state-level >70% Muslim indicator from the 1952 census, and services are globally categorized as 'federally administered' (grid electricity, flush toilets) versus 'locally administered' (pit latrines, piped water, boreholes/tubewells) without measuring state-level water statutes, State Water Boards, intergovernmental fiscal transfers, or private household self-provisioning.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate to High concern: Precolonial centralization relies on Murdock's (1967) Ethnographic Atlas (compiled from 20th-century ethnographic accounts to approximate c. 1850 institutions) intersected spatially with modern LGAs (r ~ 0.70 with self-reported ethnicity). Crucially, elite noncompliance with the 1976 military reform is proxied by a 1952 >70% Muslim state dummy, and local government quality in Table 7 is measured via subjective 2012 Afrobarometer respondent perceptions rather than objective administrative records. On the outcome side, DHS electricity availability is assumed to represent grid connection without disaggregating off-grid generators.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Adequate / Moderate concern: Potable water (piped water, borehole, tubewell, or protected well) and improved sanitation (flush toilet, VIP latrine, or pit latrine with slab) are derived from standardized nationally representative DHS household roster items across 2003-2013. However, these binary indicators capture self-reported availability rather than water safety, supply continuity, or facility functionality; DHS sampling is not stratified for representativeness at the fine 1,415 LGA-ethnic polygon level; and pooling 2003-2013 rounds into static cross-sectional means (labelled 1990-2013 in Tables 1, 4, and 5 despite Note 20 stating infrastructure data exist only for 2003-2013) obscures temporal variation in the regressions.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Some concern: No study protocol or pre-analysis plan is reported. Several robustness specifications (GCov and GTheil inequality trends, continuous centralization scores, excluding Southeast/Lagos, military president origin interactions, and non-Muslim split-sample tables) are deferred to Supplementary material or noted as 'tables available on request' (Table 4 notes; Note 53), and Note 46 indicates the >70% Muslim threshold was partly informed by exploratory multilevel regressions showing where state-specific centralization slopes turned negative.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Some concern: Although DHS household surveys are nationally representative within surveyed areas, restricting spatial regressions to the 685 of 1,415 LGA-ethnic partitions (61 of 117 Murdock ethnic groups; N = 631 complete cases in Tables 4-5) with georeferenced DHS clusters and Murdock scores, and to N = 127-162 units in the 2012 Afrobarometer regressions (Tables 6-7), introduces potential spatial selection bias. Additionally, the 1990 DHS wave omitted the Northcentral and Southsouth zones altogether (Note 13).

domain_ratings.justification: Inclusion criteria are explicitly stated at both the individual respondent level (household members aged 18 years and older in the DHS PR household roster datasets across 1990, 2003, 2008, 2010, and 2013, with infrastructure items available for 2003-2013) and the spatial regression unit level (1,415 LGA-ethnic state polygons formed by intersecting Nigeria's 774 LGAs with 117 Murdock ethnic territories, yielding 685 polygons across 61 ethnic states with matched DHS and Murdock data, and N = 631 after covariate missingness).

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
domain_ratings.justification: Core institutional and legal exposures suffer from substantial construct-validity limitations. Most critically, post-1976 elite noncompliance/rebellion against the 1976 Local Government Reform Law ('hegemonization') is not measured directly via administrative, fiscal, or conflict records; instead, it is proxied by interacting Murdock's (1967) c. 1850 precolonial centralization dummy with a state-level indicator for >70% Muslim population in the 1952 colonial census, which conflates religious demography and colonial missionary restrictions with statutory noncompliance. Furthermore, Murdock's 20th-century ethnographic coding is an imperfect proxy for c. 1850 sovereignty, and local government quality in Table 7 relies solely on subjective 2012 Afrobarometer perceptions rather than objective municipal performance metrics.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
domain_ratings.justification: While DHS household survey questions for water source (piped, borehole/tubewell, protected well) and sanitation facility (flush toilet, VIP/slab pit latrine) follow internationally standardized definitions, several measurement issues create uncertainty: (1) outcomes measure respondent-reported availability rather than functionality, water quality, or service hours (Note 14); (2) DHS does not distinguish grid from off-grid/generator electricity, which is only assumed to be grid-based (Note 25); (3) DHS surveys are not stratified to guarantee representative precision within each of the 685 sub-state LGA-ethnic polygons; and (4) Tables 1, 4, and 5 label pooled infrastructure outcomes as '1990-2013' averages even though Note 20 states infrastructure items were collected only in 2003-2013.

domain_ratings.justification: Group-weighted inequality indices (GGini, GCov, GTheil) and McKenzie's (2005) PCA wealth inequality index are appropriate for descriptive trend analysis, and Tables 4-5 appropriately cluster OLS standard errors by ethnicity (and state). However, Table 7 tests the local-governance mechanism via cross-sectional OLS of 2013 DHS outcomes on 2012 Afrobarometer perceptions (N = 135-160 LGAs) controlling only for population density—omitting the geographic, disease, and historical controls used in Equation (3) and exposing estimates to severe reverse causality—while Table 6 relies on an underpowered split sample (Cent = 1, N = 127-162) with unstable coefficients, and static pooling across uneven survey waves cannot identify dynamic historical bargaining mechanisms.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Appraised using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies, S407 raises 'Some concern' overall (with higher concern if its econometric associations are interpreted causally rather than descriptively). On the strength side, the paper clearly defines respondent and spatial-unit inclusion criteria (Q1: Yes), thoroughly characterizes Nigeria's administrative tiers, ethnic geography, and survey cohorts (Q2: Yes), uses objective cartographic and administrative boundaries validated against independent ethnicity datasets (Q4: Yes), and identifies and controls for numerous geographic, ecological, and historical slave-trade confounders in its primary spatial OLS models (Q5: Yes; Q6: Yes). Methodological concerns center on construct validity of the legal/institutional exposures (Q3: No), outcome aggregation and measurement assumptions (Q7: Unclear), and analytical limitations in the mechanism tests (Q8: Unclear). Specifically, elite noncompliance with the 1976 Local Government Reform Law is never directly observed but proxied by interacting Murdock's c. 1850 centralization indicator with a 1952 state-level >70% Muslim dummy; water and sanitation are globally labelled 'locally administered' and flush toilets 'federally administered' without measuring state water utility governance or household self-supply; spatial coverage drops from 1,415 LGA-ethnic partitions to 631 complete cases (and 135-160 LGAs in the 2012 Afrobarometer regressions); and Table 7 regresses 2013 DHS outcomes on 2012 subjective local-government perceptions controlling only for population density, leaving reverse causality and omitted confounders unaddressed. The author appropriately caveats that the OLS estimates represent correlations rather than definitive causal proof.
raw_response.study_design_identified: Quantitative observational analytical cross-sectional study (descriptive horizontal/vertical inequality decompositions across repeated cross-sectional DHS household survey waves [1990-2013; 2003-2013 for infrastructure], combined with static cross-sectional OLS regressions across spatial LGA-ethnic state partitions and LGAs)
raw_response.where_found_summary: Section 2 [PDF Pages 4-5 of 24, pp. 327-328] (geopolitical zones, LGAs, GREG/Afrobarometer ethnic validation); Section 3.1-3.2 [PDF Pages 5-6 of 24, pp. 328-329] (DHS waves, age >=18 criterion, water/sanitation/electricity definitions, GGini and McKenzie inequality equations); Section 4.1 [PDF Pages 6-7 of 24, pp. 329-330] (descriptive trends); Section 5.3-5.5 [PDF Pages 8-19 of 24, pp. 331-342] and Tables 1-7 [PDF Pages 12, 15-18 of 24, pp. 335, 338-341] (historical legal narrative, Equation 3 cross-sectional OLS specification, Murdock centralization and 1952 >70% Muslim proxy, Afrobarometer local governance regressions); Endnotes 2, 9, 12-20, 25, 45-46, 50-56 [PDF Pages 20-22 of 24, pp. 343-345] (coverage gaps, variable caveats, and sample limitations).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: S407 conducts descriptive inequality analysis across repeated cross-sectional DHS waves and tests historical/institutional hypotheses using static cross-sectional OLS regressions (Equation 3) on pooled multi-year DHS polygon means (N = 631 LGA-ethnic partitions) and single-wave 2013 DHS / 2012 Afrobarometer LGA means (N = 127-162). It employs no quasi-experimental intervention evaluation design (no DiD pre/post policy panel, IV, RDD, PSM, or ITS) and explicitly characterizes its regression findings as cross-sectional correlations (p. 342). Therefore, the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies is the exact matching tool under RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1.
